transcript.text: Let's review your comparison of smart home devices. Jack, you start.
transcript.speaker: DR PATEL

transcript.text: We borrowed all three devices from the department, so we didn't have to pay for anything ourselves.
transcript.speaker: NINA

transcript.text: That's useful. Please mention it in the methods section.
transcript.speaker: DR PATEL

transcript.text: Sure. The first is the Echo Spot, which people mostly use for setting timers in the kitchen. Its weak point is that it mishears accents quite often.
transcript.speaker: JACK

transcript.text: And the price is the best of the three, only forty-five pounds.
transcript.speaker: NINA

transcript.text: Did you test each device for the same length of time?
transcript.speaker: DR PATEL

transcript.text: Yes, we tested every device in my flat, and then in Nina's, to get a fair comparison.
transcript.speaker: JACK

transcript.text: Mm. What about the second device?
transcript.speaker: DR PATEL

transcript.text: That's the Lumos thermostat. People buy it to control heating from their phones, mainly to save money in winter. The problem is the app crashes during updates.
transcript.speaker: NINA

transcript.text: It's also the most expensive, ninety pounds. Though last month there was a discount, eighty.
transcript.speaker: JACK

transcript.text: Our flatmates helped a lot, to be honest. They kept giving the devices strange commands to see what would happen.
transcript.speaker: NINA

transcript.text: That sounds like a good informal test. Did they find anything surprising?
transcript.speaker: DR PATEL

transcript.text: They found that one of the devices answers questions in a very polite way, which made everyone laugh.
transcript.speaker: JACK

transcript.text: And the third? I understand you tested a smart doorbell.
transcript.speaker: DR PATEL

transcript.text: Yes, the camera one. We wanted to see if it really improves security.
transcript.speaker: JACK

transcript.text: In our test, it sent alerts for every passing car, so we turned the sensitivity down. After that it was reliable.
transcript.speaker: NINA

transcript.text: Did you consider privacy?
transcript.speaker: DR PATEL

transcript.text: We also noticed that the doorbell uses a lot of battery power, so you have to charge it quite often.
transcript.speaker: JACK

transcript.text: That's worth mentioning as a practical point for users.
transcript.speaker: DR PATEL

transcript.text: A little. Some users worry the video is stored on company servers. We recommend reading the privacy policy before buying, though honestly few people do.
transcript.speaker: JACK

transcript.text: Fair. Overall, which would you recommend to a student?
transcript.speaker: DR PATEL

transcript.text: The speaker, definitely. It's cheap and flexible. The thermostat only makes sense if you own your home, and most students rent.
transcript.speaker: NINA

transcript.text: I disagree slightly. I'd say the doorbell is more useful for shared houses, but I accept it costs too much for most of us.
transcript.speaker: JACK

transcript.text: Good. That kind of disagreement is useful, because it shows that you've considered different users.
transcript.speaker: DR PATEL

transcript.text: We wanted the report to show both points of view, not just one opinion.
transcript.speaker: NINA

transcript.text: Interesting. For your final report, what will you add?
transcript.speaker: DR PATEL

transcript.text: A section on energy use, because a device that's always listening uses electricity all day.
transcript.speaker: NINA

transcript.text: And a short survey of fifty users, if we have time.
transcript.speaker: JACK

transcript.text: Keep it realistic. A survey is a big job. Focus on the energy section first.
transcript.speaker: DR PATEL

transcript.text: We'll also include a table with the results from the flats, so readers can see the details easily.
transcript.speaker: JACK

transcript.text: Excellent. Clear presentation always earns extra marks.
transcript.speaker: DR PATEL

transcript.text: Understood. We'll send the plan tomorrow.
transcript.speaker: NINA
